key_features.classic_presentation: Acute cholecystitis presents with right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain that develops over hours, often after a fatty meal. Pain is constant and severe. Murphy's sign (arrest of inspiration during RUQ palpation) is highly specific. Fever and nausea are common.
key_features.typical_demographics: More common in females (4:1 ratio). Risk factors: 4 F's - Female, Forty, Fat, Fertile. However, can occur in any demographic with gallstones.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Obstruction of cystic duct by gallstone leads to gallbladder inflammation, distension, and potential necrosis/perforation if untreated.

diagnostic_questions.context: RUQ location is highly specific for cholecystitis. Pain may radiate to right shoulder/scapula.
Cholecystitis often triggered by fatty meal. Pain develops over 1-6 hours and becomes constant.
Cholecystitis pain is constant (unlike biliary colic which is intermittent). Lasting > 6 hours is typical.
Fever present in 35-40% of cholecystitis. High fever may indicate complications.
Nausea/vomiting common (70%) but non-specific. Persistent vomiting may indicate complications.
Right shoulder/scapular radiation (Kehr's sign) occurs in 60% due to diaphragmatic irritation.
Most present within 24 hours of onset. Symptoms > 7 days suggest chronic cholecystitis.
History of biliary colic (intermittent RUQ pain) common. Acute-on-chronic presentation is typical.

differential_diagnosis.key_difference: Intermittent pain (not constant), resolves within 6 hours, no fever
Epigastric (not RUQ), radiates to back, amylase/lipase elevated
Jaundice, darker urine, more gradual onset

red_flags.action: Possible choledocholithiasis or Mirizzi syndrome - immediate ER

typical_management: Urgent surgical consultation. NPO (nothing by mouth). IV antibiotics. Cholecystectomy typically within 72 hours of symptom onset. Delayed surgery increases complication risk.
disposition: Emergency department for urgent surgical evaluation. Most require hospital admission and cholecystectomy.
patient_education: Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder, usually caused by a gallstone blocking the duct. It requires surgery to remove the gallbladder. Without treatment, it can lead to serious complications including infection, gangrene, or rupture.
